quotes.excerpt: Land of Never #1 is a nice start to a very promising series. The initial premise will grab your attention, but the teased tie in will make you sit up in your seat. The artwork is fantastic and leaves nothing to the imagination as it captures the story completely. This is a must grab at the shop this week. Give this first issue a shot and consider adding it to your Pull List, or at the very least order the second issue to see where it goes.

Land of Never takes a familiar tale and twists it into something truly unsettling. Steve Orlando delivers a gripping mystery fueled by a desperate father, all while Miguel Mora illustrates atmospheric tension that jumps from the page. Land of Never is the version of an age-old classic that you never knew you needed, a blend of heart and horror. Cannot wait for what is coming next.

Conan The Barbarian #33 sets sail when Conan and the Red Brotherhood are shipwrecked on a mysterious island after encountering a massive storm and a supernatural attacker. Jim Zub’s start to the latest arc is as strong as ever, and Fernando Dagnino’s artwork is a perfect fit. 10 out of 10. No notes.

This was a solid issue that carries a real sense of danger and presents readers with a problem that only someone like James T. Kirk could likely solve. There is also a great observation made by both Kirk and Jurati about Sato, which has been a recurring theme throughout the series so far. Sato is a captain who is often held back from making the tough choices because of his own fears and self-doubt.
Gonzalez delivers stunning art throughout the issue. I absolutely love the character designs and the attention to detail in every page and panel.

X-Men #34 is a strong character study of the Juggernaut, getting by on carefully crafted scriptwriting. With MacKay shifting to more solo stories as X-Men races toward DNX, here's hoping that he and future collaborators keep digging deep into what makes the X-Men tick.

X-Men #34 is a soft analysis of the current state of the Juggernaut rather than a deep dive into his character. The issue is meant to challenge him more than it’s meant to give any kind of exposé on the character’s past as a villain. All in all, it reads like something readers have seen before and is simple but has its nuance to a point.

Kingdom of Earth builds an unsettling world while introducing us to some horrific monsters and a protagonist worth rooting for. David Dastmalchian, Leah Kilpatrick, and Soo Lee craft a grim and brutal apocalyptic world that leaves us eager for what happens next. Kingdom of Earth is a brutal, monster-filed story balancing relentless darkness with a glimpse of hope.

Dastmalchian and Kilpatrick craft a dark, engaging and thrilling story in this first issue. One of the things that draws me into a story is world building and this first issue creates an interesting and unique world that I want to see explored. I like the mystery of the world itself and how the factions deal with the limitations of their power. There are some interesting characters littered throughout this first issue and I am on board with both the premise and the world of this series.

While this series has just four issues and that might not seem like a lot of space to tell such an intense tale, The Horror of Godzilla #1 has already set things up for horrific greatness. You’re never going to look at the King of the Monsters the same way again.

The Horror of Godzilla #1 is exactly what the title promises, an incredibly terrifying look at the King of the Monsters through the eyes of those caught in their path. Writers Ethan S. Parker and Griffin Sheridan deliver on of the most unsettling Godzilla stories I have ever experienced, while Tristan Jones brings his A-game with artwork that is both impactful and horrifying. The Horror of Godzilla is one of the most frightening Godzilla stories with some of the best illustrations I have seen in recent memory, making it a strong contender for comic of the year.
Something is Killing the Children #48 delivers yet another strong issue, balancing action, emotion, and world-building with real confidence. Thrilling from start to finish. A great read.

A difficult conversation between Erica and Jessica reveals a new side to the life of the Order in a powerful chapter. Tynion IV delves into Jessica’s deep pain with magnificent writing . Dell’edera and Muerto unload the heavy burdens of truth with impressive visuals. The world of Erica Slaughter is one that never leaves readers thoughts when the issue finishes for a reason.

A tragic past reveal sparks an explosive search for present day answers as Batman is on the hunt! Taylor pens a striking tale of loss and heart in this latest chapter. Janín exposes the a hero’s last moments with stunning art. This series never falters on delivering high marks.
Detective Comics #1111 ramps up the action and mystery in the latest issue, while also showcasing the great potential of having Batman team up with additional heroes.

Superman #40 wraps up one big event, leads us into another, and hints at the future for Superboy Prime. With Clark Kent set to return soon, Prime won’t be front and center, but I think he’s shown that he can be a more than average substitute for the Man of Steel.
Williamson, Mora and Sanchez roll the dice in walking a fine line of genius and insanity with CK’s heroic methods. Another display of high level storytelling for a very polarizing character.

Operation: Iron Coffin comes out of the gate swinging with a unique premise that delivers far more than ever expected. Kenny Porter and Tyrell Cannon give us a Dracula that isn’t just here for the carnage, although we get plenty of that, but for a compelling redemption arc wrapped in a fast-paced, blood-soaked WWII setting. IDW Dark may have some heavy hitting titles in its first year as an imprint at IDW Publishing, but Operation: Iron Coffin stands out as one of the best.

Operation Coffin #1 is a stylish debut for Porter and Cannon’s new take on Dracula. A truly unique premise, backed by engaging lore and a curious mission have already laid the groundwork for a wild ride ahead.

Detective Comics #1111 ramps up the action and mystery in the latest issue, while also showcasing the great potential of having Batman team up with additional heroes.

The Uncanny X-Men #32 brings this out-of-this-world arc to an end and we’re left on a very interesting note of uncertainty, sadness, and love. Gail Simone makes you feel every emotion and leaves you wanting more.

When the Nur try wiping out the Brood, they forgot what party they crashed! Simone’s writing balances the heartfelt drama with outright fun themes. The art centers in on the chaotic scene with great success. This has been such a refreshing change of pace story that reminds fans to push the creative boundaries on the stat quo X-tales.

An origin story centered around one of the main book’s killers could have easily gone sideways, but thankfully that’s simply not the case with Rascal Randy. Instead, fans have an up-close look at several compelling characters and insight into one of the most unpredictable and twisted characters in comics.

If you finished Exquisite Corpses Season 1 wanting more from Rascal Randy, this new series is exactly what you had hope for. Tyler Boss expands on the history of the character without taking away some of the mystery in the main series. Boss delivers a creepy, atmospheric story that stands confidently on its own while adding to the lore Exquisite Corpses. Exquisite Corpses: Rascal Randy is one of those rare prequels that doesn’t just justify its existence, it makes an already iconic character even more fascinating.

The Flash #35 is another winning chapter that reminds readers why Wally West remains one of DC's most endearing heroes. Ryan North balances inventive superhero concepts with genuine heart, while Gavin Guidry's artwork radiates personality from start to finish. The central idea of preventing disasters before they happen opens up exciting possibilities, and the creative team wisely leaves enough uncertainty to keep you wondering where it all leads. Even before the larger questions arrive, this issue succeeds by making heroism feel joyful, hopeful, and endlessly fun.

Wally West’s obsession with the future leads to more hijinks as events speed along. North leans heavily into the scientific portion of plans with the writing. Guidry and Lucas craft solid looks at this new scheme via the art. An interesting take leading into more fast problems down the road. Don’t miss out.

I’m sure some of the rhetoric in this issue, particularly out of Mia’s mouth, will get a lot of people talking about certain real-world parallels, but this comic actually works really well justin the context of a superhero story. This is a world where the innocent are hunted and the guilty are more powerful than ever, and the heroes are often powerless to strike back – so villain tactics might be necessary to fight back.

Absolute Green Arrow #2 takes us deeper into the mystery of who our killer is. This issue brings us to familiar faces within the Green Arrow lore and shrouds us in mystery even more than before. The blend of action and suspense is working cleverly, making this a horror story of sorts. I will have this run at the very top of my pull pile every month; I hope it gets expanded beyond its current limited run.

From the deep messages and fantastic storytelling to the excellent and varied art & colors, “Justice League Dream Girls” continues to astound! Maines and Axelrod continue to prove they put their souls into their writing while Wilson more than delivers on a fantastic Harlivy side story. This is a fantastic series that you won’t want to miss!

The interaction between Galaxy and the 1st transgender superhero Coagula is an utterly iconic mentoring and banter moment and truly empowers Galaxy to speak up for herself and Dreamer. It’s also a lovely homage to Coagula’s co-creator, the late Rachel Pollack. It’s also so damn relatable that Galaxy is overwhelmed by all the screens around her: a true superhero vulnerability for 2026.
If Destruction Be Our Lot #2 continues to flesh out its weird, wild, and wonderful world of robots, by offering plenty of visuals with personality and plot twists that will have readers talking.

I already require the next issue of “If Destruction Be Our Lot” to be in my hands. This issue continues an already going trend of the Rosenberg brothers, MacDonald and Segala creating something truly once-in-a-lifetime. This series could really teach us a thing or two.

Absolute Batman #21 is another huge triumph for Scott Snyder and the team. It navigates a number of different setups between huge action set pieces, a rather grand funeral and a slightly twisted finale to setup a number of huge storylines for year three of the Absolute initiative.

Ever since the original Batman run, Scott Snyder’s Joker has always been among the scariest I’ve ever read, but this is on a whole other level. The level of disturbing visuals by Nick Dragotta work absolutely perfectly to end the issue with literal shivers down your spine.
Nightwing #139 strays away from the overly upbeat tone Nightwing is stereotyped into having.

Nightwing may not be the flashiest title on the stands today. However, this issue proves that it can still surprise even a jaded reader with something special. I can’t say anything beyond that without spoiling it, but I loved this issue!

Geiger #24 brings the series back in a big way. Revealing a new threat while continuing the journey with a group we’ve fallen in love with gives this issue some real bite. The story is so good it almost makes you forget about the inconsistencies with the releases of the issues in this series. Geiger still stands out as the flagship series from Ghost Machine and that is not a bad thing at all. If you haven’t been reading Geiger, this is a perfect jump on point. So, grab a copy when you are at the shop this week and get lost in the world of the Glowing Man.

Much like Geiger, I’m still processing what happened with the Northerner, and what it all means. This issue moves along the story, and shows there is something big coming, and it’s all connected. Geiger continues to be a superb comic with action, gorgeous art, and a story that keeps you on your toes!

This series often errs a little too much on the side of purely silly – both in terms of the villains and in terms of Harley’s current bizarre identity crisis – but this issue shows that the creative team really has a great action scene or two tucked away in their back pockets.
Harley Quinn #64 sets up the final chapter of "The Harq Knight Returns" with wild action, humorous callbacks, gritty and colorful action and a wild cliffhanger.

Conan The Barbarian #33 sets sail when Conan and the Red Brotherhood are shipwrecked on a mysterious island after encountering a massive storm and a supernatural attacker. Jim Zub’s start to the latest arc is as strong as ever, and Fernando Dagnino’s artwork is a perfect fit. 10 out of 10. No notes.

Overall, Feral #25 is one of the most exciting issues of the series to date, one that is filled with lots of suspense, action, and dread. The issue serves as an effective conclusion to the Feral/Stray Dogs crossover, and sets the stage for what is sure to be an exciting new arc for the series.

The CDC mayhem comes to an explosive end with the unified front of Cats and Dogs on the defensive. Fleecs pens a highly driven tale with strong horror elements in place. Forstner and the team keep readers on edge with the frantic chaos swirling the panels. A superb display of storytelling that hits a bullseye each time.

The Brutal Dark is poised to strike but Ezra Cain is flying into the heart of danger in this exciting chapter. Condon wraps up events  with a direct shot of intensity. Phillips’ art takes readers on a roller-coaster ride of emotions.  A great “so long for now”, but definitely not “goodbye forever”.
While the finale feels a little abrupt, Peril of the Brutal Dark: An Ezra Cain Mystery #6 is still a great final issue for one of the best series of the year.

This issue doesn’t feature the DEO’s mysterious new magical enforcer, leaving that plot hanging a little longer, but it’s a a great little done-in-one that shows us how Zatanna is operating in her new role. It’s more like we’ve been invited along for one of her shows, except that this time the show is about the magical structure of the universe.

If someone hasn’t been reading the current Zatanna run, this might be a good place to pick it up. It doesn’t give a recap of the story so far, but it does explain just what being the Prime Magus entails.

This second issue continues to build on a plot that provides luring mystery. Making readers question many different aspects of this story. Which leaves them hooked within the narrative and plot of this story. Will Frank finally snap? What is Bruce’s real motive for getting the cube? And will Spider-Man be able to stop whatever is to come…? After only two issues this is a very intriguing story that I am excited to see what happens next! Get this newest issue of Spider-Man: Long Way Home today from your local comic book shop!

Spider-Man: Long Way Home #2 continues to impress thanks to Adam Kubert's commanding artwork and Jonathan Hickman's cinematic approach visually, but the story moves at a deliberate pace. The issue invests heavily in atmosphere, framing, and character positioning, particularly with Punisher and Bruce Banner, though Spider-Man himself remains surprisingly absent for long stretches. There are intriguing ideas at work, especially around the Cosmic Cube and Banner's unsettling role, but readers may wish the narrative covered more ground before the final page.

Kyle vs. the internet … round one….FIGHT! Adams puts Rayner in a most comical situation as a downer of being a celebrity comes to his front door. The art shines in its’ expressions of the often humorous moments before the show stoppign finale page. Hollywood is never a boring time.

Green Lantern #37 leans into character development over spectacle, giving Kyle Rayner another enjoyable chapter as he adjusts to life in Los Angeles. Jeremy Adams continues to build Kyle's supporting cast and relationships while planting intriguing seeds for larger stories ahead. Although the main villain doesn't leave much of an impact, the issue's charm and final-page surprise help keep the momentum rolling.

reason.snippet: Vampire Survivors #1 understands exactly what fans enjoy about the game and translates that energy into comics with impressive confidence. David Hazan keeps the momentum high while Jimmy Kucaj delivers expressive characters, inventive action sequences, and pages overflowing with monsters. Readers unfamiliar with the source material may wish for more context before the battles begin, but the sheer…
pros: Jimmy Kucaj's energetic artwork brings the nonstop action to life.
Creative layouts and Joao Canola's vibrant colors amplify the chaotic battles.
Successfully recreates the frantic feel of the video game.
cons: Character development and story takes a backseat to the action.
The rapid pace leaves little room to establish emotional stakes.

reason.snippet: Fiery, feisty, and fun! This anthology series is filled to the gills with unique POVs of familiar and lesser-known heroes to check out that's tonally a perfect celebration of summer and its sunny disposition.
pros: I loved this ensemble of talents artist and writers rallying to make this issue a reality. The different flavors and choose-your-own-adventure of stories, with…
immediate sass and fourth-wall breaks with Hawkgirl’s inaugural tale where she allies with Catwoman to take down the Lord of Darkness and Disorder makes this a…
A fun melange of art styles that are dynamic instead of clash with each other

reason.snippet: The Patron #1 is a cool, horror-esque take of an up and coming artist meeting their untimely death. John J. Pearson artwork brings an amazingly eerie feel to this book with compositions that art right out of a film. Christian Ward’s writing drags a bit at times but sets it up well for the next issue.
pros: John J. Pearson’s artwork ties everything together for an intense, eerie feel.
Christian Ward’s use of foreshadowing makes it interesting to keep reading.
cons: The story feels repetitive at times and drags while the main characters meet with Mr. Cherish

reason.snippet: Bishop #2 features solid artwork and good action moments, but the expository dialogue and inner monologue really holds it back.
pros: The art by Mario Santoro and Reese Hannigan does a great job with the storytelling.
The dialogue between Bishop and Shard really sells the sibling relationship.
cons: While there's potential to make the motivation of this Final Brotherhood compelling, it hasn't happened yet.
The structure of the series is a bit rote.

reason.snippet: This book has one of the best combinations of X-characters ever and is filled with some great character moments and a thrilling (and surprisingly bloody) climactic battle.
pros: The Australian setting and personalities of this diverse mix of X-characters is captured wonderfully by artist Stephen Segovia.
Writer Steve Orlando gives each of the characters time to shine while dropping in subplots with omens of bigger menaces to come.
I loved how Dazzler's worried about her career by being out of the public eye, which I imagine a huge pop star would feel in the real world.

reason.snippet: Queen in Black #1 fires on all cylinders as an event opener, establishing enormous stakes while never losing sight of the characters caught in the middle. Al Ewing balances cosmic spectacle with sharp pacing, giving readers plenty of action, memorable hero moments, and intriguing mysteries without making the oversized issue feel bloated. Paired with Iban Coello's stunning visuals, this is the kind…
pros: Excellent balance of blockbuster action and character moments
Iban Coello's artwork is consistently spectacular
Oversized issue delivers strong value with multiple memorable sequences
cons: Large cast limits meaningful page time for several heroes

reason.snippet: Queen in Black: Defenders of Light and Dark #1 embraces the blockbuster energy readers expect from a Marvel event tie-in. Al Ewing and Tom Waltz make smart use of two distinct teams, giving every hero a chance to contribute while planting seeds that could have meaningful implications for the larger crossover. Although the issue prioritizes action over quieter character moments, the focus on Cloak…
pros: Creative Team Light and Team Dark lineups make every battle feel fresh.
Cloak and Dagger emerge as the emotional anchor of the story.
Beta Ray Bill's connection to current Mortal Thor continuity adds welcome depth.
cons: Character development takes a backseat to nearly nonstop action.
Hela and Knull function more as imposing obstacles than memorable personalities.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Spectacular Spider-Man: Brand New Day #3 keeps upping the stakes, delivering plenty of action and surprise twists as Spidey's battle against the corrupted Punisher continues. It also boasts some of the best art in a Spider-Man comic to date, making it worth the cover price.
pros: Slott perfectly raises the stakes in Spidey's battle with Mister Negative.
To's artwork remains top notch, capturing Spidey's agility and the Punisher's seemingly endless arsenal.
A opening page by Marcos Martin delivers one of the best pieces of art I've seen in a comic this year.
Great use of colors by Alex Sinclair, especially since black and white is a defining theme.

reason.label: AIPT review
reason.snippet: Action Comics #1100 serves as both a celebration of Superman's history and a look at his next steps, thanks to some of the best creators in comics.
pros: Waid and Patridge balance Clark Kent's teenage woes with a threat that spans all of time and space.
Ryan Sook reinterprets key moments in Superman history while also building on the main story.
Backup stories not only pick up on the end of DC K.O., but touch on all of the members of the Superman family.
cons: The last story is more or less set-up for the upcoming storyline.

Gail Simone ensures the team's newest members earn their place through courage and leadership, while the emotional final pages set an exciting course for what's next. The climactic battle doesn't always capitalize on its biggest moments, though, with several action beats rushing past…
pros: The Outliers each get opportunities to shine and evolve.
Gail Simone balances multiple characters without losing momentum.
cons: The alien conflict wraps up a bit too abruptly.
Last four pages are devoted to setting up the Outliers going forward.
